D.t: N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas trails by 19.7 and wins 0% of simulations. Closing it takes about 128,806 voters switching sides, or 257,611 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +26.6 and R +12.4. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Oklahoma, a projected net 31,679 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Tulsa, R +6.3, 16.8% of the vote; Cleveland, R +0.4, 7.8% of the vote; Comanche, R +4.4, 2.2% of the vote; Payne, R +9.5, 2.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas runs furthest behind in Washington, Wagoner, Mayes. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 35 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.27 points; Voters without a degree, 63% of voters, 36 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.15 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 58% of voters, 40 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.89 points.

The forecast's worst groups for N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas: Immigration voters 14 to 77, Incomes $125K and up 25 to 66, Small counties 25 to 66. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
